name: Future Skills interest questionnaire
attribution: 36 activity statements written for Future Skills, six for each of Holland's six interest types (RIASEC), the model behind O*NET's interest profiles. Not the O*NET Interest Profiler; scores are compared with O*NET 31.0 occupation interest profiles (CC BY 4.0).
stem: How much would you enjoy doing this at work?

types.R: Realistic: hands-on work with tools, machines, plants or animals
types.I: Investigative: finding things out, analysing, solving problems
types.S: Social: helping, teaching, caring for people
types.E: Enterprising: leading, persuading, selling, starting things
types.C: Conventional: organising data, records and procedures

items.text: Repair a motorcycle or car engine.
Run experiments in a laboratory.
Design posters, logos or social media graphics.
Teach or tutor children or adults.
Start and run your own small business.
Keep accounts and check that the numbers balance.
Operate machines on a factory production line.
Find out why a machine or a program keeps failing.
Write stories, articles or scripts.
Care for patients in a hospital or clinic.
Persuade people to buy a product or service.
Organise files, records and schedules.
Plant, grow and harvest crops on a farm or plantation.
Study how diseases spread and how to stop them.
Take photographs or edit videos.
Help people work through personal or family problems.
Lead a team and make decisions for it.
Enter and check data in a spreadsheet or system.
Build furniture or install shelves and cabinets.
Analyse data to find patterns and explain them.
Act, sing or perform in front of an audience.
Coach a sports team or train new staff.
Negotiate a deal or a contract.
Follow set rules and procedures to process applications.
Wire and test electrical circuits in a building.
Read research to understand how something works.
Plan how a room, building or garden should look.
Organise volunteers for a community project.
Plan a marketing campaign for a new product.
Check documents for errors and missing information.
Drive a lorry or operate a crane at a work site.
Test water or soil samples for pollution.
Create characters and scenes for an animation or a game.
Help customers find what they need and solve their problems.
Speak for your organisation at events and meetings.
Track stock and orders in a warehouse or shop.
